title: Pancho the brave dog
summary: Pancho is terribly scared of storms. But one night, in the middle of the worst one ever, he hears a meow in the garden.

scenes.text:
Pancho was a small dog with long floppy ears and a white patch on his nose that looked like spilled milk.

He liked balls, puddles, and being scratched behind the ear. He was the friendliest dog on the whole street.

But he had a secret.

He was scared of storms. A huge kind of scared, far too big to fit inside such a small dog.

As soon as the sky turned grey, Pancho could feel it in his paws. And the moment the sky began to rumble, he shot under the bed and didn't come out until it was all over.

One autumn night, the worst storm of the year arrived.

It began with the sky turning black. Then came a wind that made the windows creak. And then it broke open completely: rain drumming on the roof like a thousand drums, and lightning painting the walls white.

Pancho was already under the bed, curled into a ball, eyes squeezed shut.

Then, over all the noise, came the thunder.

The biggest he had ever heard in his life.

Pancho trembled from his nose to his tail.

And right afterwards, as that great crash died away, he heard something else. Something tiny and high that wasn't rain or wind.

It was coming from the garden.

It was a meow.

Pancho opened one eye.

Out there, in the middle of all that, was a kitten. Alone. Getting soaked.

"I can't," thought Pancho, pressing himself flatter against the floor. "It's stormy."

But the kitten called out again, quieter, more tired.

Pancho gulped. He crawled out from under the bed. He crossed the hall on trembling legs. He pushed open the kitchen door with his nose, the one that led to the garden, and looked out.

The rain soaked him in a second. A flash of lightning left him blinking.

But Pancho kept going. Sniffing, step by step, all the way to the bush at the very end.

There was the kitten, curled up tight, shivering.

And Pancho, who had never been brave, gathered up all the courage he had, and barked.

It wasn't to frighten it. It was to say: here I am, come with me.

The kitten understood. It came out of the bush and pressed itself against his side, and like that, together, both of them dripping, they went back to the house.

Pancho's mum found them in the kitchen, puddles all around them. She didn't say a word. She just brought a big towel, dried them both, and settled them into Pancho's bed, next to the fire.

Outside the storm went on. The sky kept on rumbling.

But the kitten snuggled up against Pancho's tummy and began to purr. A small, warm purr that tickled.

And Pancho noticed something: he was still scared. But now he had someone to look after, and that was bigger.

Little by little, with the rain on the roof, the two of them fell asleep.
